proof_summary: For \(N=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}-1\), modular binary exponentiation in \(\mathbb Z[\sqrt3]/N\), using \(N+1=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}\), shows that \(2+\sqrt3\) has exact order \(N+1\) in \(((\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)[\sqrt3])^\times\) for every prime \(p\mid N\), with the proper-order checks corresponding to the prime divisors \(2,3,100943\). Hence \(N+1<p^2\) for every prime divisor \(p\) of \(N\), contradicting \(p^2\le N\) for the least prime factor if \(N\) were composite; thus \(N\) is prime and \(m=39101\) supplies a positive witness.
